item.title: Beyond the IDE: Running Autonomous Agentic SDLC in Isolated Containers
item.description:
Beyond the IDE: Running Autonomous Agentic SDLC in Isolated Containers

In Part 1 and Part 2, I shared the governance rules that keep AI coding agents on track: Dual-PR Spec-First contracts and the adaptive L0–L3 auto mode.

However, one practical problem remained: everything still runs on the developer’s laptop.

If an agent needs 10 minutes to run tests, explore AST files, and do a review pass, the developer has to keep their laptop awake, avoid switching branches, and baby-sit terminal prompts. If you try to run agents in standard CI, they either crash when asking for interactive input or make wild guesses.

item.title: Scaling Agentic SDLC: Designing an Adaptive Auto Mode for Autonomous Coding
item.description:
Scaling Agentic SDLC: Designing an Adaptive Auto Mode for Autonomous Coding

In Part 1, I explained why moving from AI-first prompt engineering (VS Code + GitHub Copilot / OpenCode) to autonomous agentic coding (VS Code + Claude Code) breaks traditional software delivery, and why I built a strict Dual-PR Spec-First workflow for autonomous agents. By separating intent agreement from implementation execution, the architectural results were solid: zero contract drift, no test gaming, and strict boundary containment.

item.title: From AI-First + SDD to Agentic SDLC: Building a Dual-PR Governance Engine for Autonomous Coding
item.description:
From AI-First + SDD to Agentic SDLC: Building a Dual-PR Governance Engine for Autonomous Coding

Over the past three years, software engineering underwent two quiet revolutions.

First came the AI-Assisted era. Tools like early GitHub Copilot delivered inline tab-completions. The developer remained the compiler, the architect, and the typist—AI was simply an intelligent autocomplete.

Then came the AI-First era, powered by Spec-Driven Development (SDD). Senior engineers quickly realized that casual, conversational prompting produced fragile code. To get production-grade output from large language models in environments like VS Code + GitHub Copilot and VS Code + OpenCode, the industry converged on a disciplined methodology: write formal specifications first. We learned to draft Markdown PRDs, define OpenAPI schemas, and document BDD scenarios (GIVEN / WHEN / THEN) before asking the model to write code. Feeding structured specifications into the model allowed teams to generate entire modules, database schemas, and integration suites cleanly. For teams practicing SDD, AI-first development became the gold standard of productivity.

item.title: What Claude Code's Source Code Taught Me About Building Production AI Agents
item.description:
Why Read Source Code?

Most writing about AI agents describes patterns in the abstract. Clean Mermaid diagrams, idealised loops, production-sounding words. None of it tells you how the system behaves when the LLM hallucinates a field name, or what happens when a Bash command runs for 20 seconds, or how you prevent a child agent from bankrupting your token budget.

I read the source code of Anthropic’s Claude Code — a production CLI agent shipped to real engineers daily — and traced every architectural decision back to its implementation. What follows are the patterns worth understanding before you design your next agentic system.

item.title: Building Production Agentic AI: Patterns, Evals, and Architecture Trade-offs
item.description:
Building Production Agentic AI: Patterns, Evals, and Architecture Trade-offs

Why This Guide Matters

If you’ve shipped LLM-based features, you’ve probably hit the wall where simple prompt engineering stops working. Your PM wants the AI to “do more,” your team is drowning in edge cases, and you’re not sure if you need better prompts, more tools, or an entirely different architecture.

I’ve been there. After building several production agentic systems, here’s what I wish someone had told me on day one: The difference between teams that ship working AI agents and those that don’t isn’t the model—it’s the discipline around evaluation and error analysis.
